pool.text: The Domesday Book contained the first record of the settlement at Plymouth.
The name Plym Mouth was first mentioned in a Pipe Roll.
Plympton Priory secured a royal charter granting the right to hold a weekly market.
A French attack burned a manor house and took some prisoners during the war.
Breton raiders burned the town.
Sutton was incorporated as a borough and formally renamed Plymouth.
The borough was granted city status.
Burrator Reservoir, located north of the city, was expanded.
King George V granted the city the dignity of Lord Mayor.
Charles Church was hit by incendiary bombs during the Blitz.
Sir Patrick Abercrombie's Plan to rebuild the bomb-damaged city was published.
Michael Foot was elected Labour MP for the constituency of Plymouth Devonport.
The Pannier Market was completed inside a grade II listed building.
The modernist high rise of the Civic Centre was constructed.
Plymouth City Council was formally twinned with Brest, France.
City boundaries expanded to include Plympton and Plymstock.
The South West Water Authority was formed by the Water Act.
Plymouth City Council was formally twinned with Gdynia, Poland.
The water industry was privatised and Plymouth has been supplied by South West Water.
The world record for the most simultaneous fireworks was surpassed.
